questions.q: Is Castellan Industrial Group, used in this case study, a real company?
options: Yes, it's a real Fortune 500 manufacturer
Yes, it's a real company but anonymized
No — it's explicitly a fictional, illustrative composite used to apply the course's concepts
It's a real company that the lesson declines to name
questions.explain: The lesson states directly: 'This is a realistic composite of the kind of problem this course exists to solve — not a real company's data.'

questions.q: Why did Castellan reject a fully centralized governance operating model?
options: Centralized models cannot be documented with ADRs
No central team could realistically own data definitions for twenty plants running three different ERPs on day one
The board explicitly forbade any central standards at all
Centralized models are illegal for manufacturers
questions.explain: The scale and system diversity made full centralization unrealistic, so Castellan chose federated governance instead.

questions.q: What was the core metadata architecture challenge in this case study?
options: The board refused to fund any metadata work
All twenty plants used the exact same ERP already
The company had no data of any kind
Plant-floor OT data and corporate IT/financial data had never shared a catalog
questions.explain: The hardest technical problem was bridging operational technology data and corporate financial data into one coherent enterprise metadata architecture.

questions.q: Why did the platform decision in Chapter 4 get written up as its own ADR?
options: ADRs are only used for security incidents
It was an expensive, hard-to-reverse choice that needed a recorded reason
ADRs are required for every minor software setting
The board requested a PowerPoint instead
questions.explain: Choosing one enterprise catalog over standardizing on a single ERP vendor's tools was exactly the kind of significant, hard-to-reverse decision Lesson 25 says deserves an ADR.

questions.q: According to the case study's result, why did the fix work after eighteen months?
options: Federation gave each plant room to keep its own tools while agreeing to one shared definition for the metrics that mattered
The board stopped asking for a consistent view
Every plant was forced onto identical software
All regional divisions were shut down except one
questions.explain: The result wasn't uniformity of tools — it was agreement on a small set of shared, board-critical metric definitions.
